bib.title: Chapter 1: Introducing Gen AI and the Role of Data (Generative AI and LLMs For Dummies, Snowflake Special Edition)
bib.venue: John Wiley & Sons, Inc. (Snowflake Special Edition)

question: What is the historical context of generative AI and why does enterprise data, managed on a cloud data platform, matter for gen AI projects?
contributions: Brief history of AI from rule-based systems to transformers and LLMs
Argument that enterprise data is the differentiator for gen AI
Pitch for a cloud data platform to manage gen AI projects

results.claim: Transformer architecture was introduced by the Google Brain team in 2017, per a Forbes article cited by the chapter.
results.source: Forbes, 'Transformers Revolutionized AI. What Will Replace Them?'
results.setup: History of LLMs; attributed to Forbes article 'Transformers Revolutionized AI. What Will Replace Them?'
results.quote: a key breakthrough came in 2017 when the Google Brain team introduced the transformer architecture
results.note: Attribution to Google Brain; the transformer paper (Vaswani et al.) is not named.

results.claim: 80 to 90 percent of data is unstructured.
results.source: MIT, 'Tapping the Power of Unstructured Data', Feb 2021
results.setup: Enterprise data in general; MIT report Feb 2021
results.quote: 80 to 90 percent of data is unstructured

results.claim: Training commercial foundation models costs tens of millions of dollars; adapting one costs a fraction.
results.setup: Commercial foundation models; no model or year given
results.quote: Training these commercial foundation models is an immense effort that costs tens of millions of dollars.

results.claim: LLM training data is typically measured in petabytes (defined as a million gigabytes).
results.quote: Successful LLMs are trained on enormous data sets typically measured in petabytes
results.note: Unsourced and likely overstated: text pretraining corpora are usually terabytes. The 'million gigabytes' gloss for a petabyte is correct (decimal).

results.claim: Larger LLMs may incorporate hundreds of billions of parameters.
results.source: CNN, 'Microsoft confirms it's investing billions in the creator of ChatGPT'
results.setup: Progressively larger LLMs, cited to CNN article
results.quote: some of which may incorporate hundreds of billions of parameters

limits: Vendor (Snowflake) promotional chapter for a general audience; no experiments, no method detail.
Authors are not printed in this chapter excerpt.
Claims are mostly unsourced or cite news articles rather than primary papers.

Dated: names ChatGPT as 'chatbot generative pre-trained transformer' (wrong expansion: GPT is generative pre-trained transformer), says Twitter is 'formerly' X, and says nothing of RAG, agents, reasoning models or post-2023 developments.
practices: Combine first-, second- and third-party data to build a complete data set for gen AI (p.6 and sidebar).
Adapt an existing pretrained foundation model rather than training from scratch (p.9).
Unify enterprise data in one governed repository with a single copy of data (p.9-10).
Use a managed cloud data platform and scale GPUs for training, fine-tuning and inference (p.10).
Augment LLMs with corporate data in a secure and governed manner (p.9).
